correctness.rationale: The coordinatewise mean-value bound and the directional derivatives at ze_j give the Lipschitz norm C; uniform convergence of the finite-coordinate holomorphic maps on the ball yields holomorphy. Each truncation has bounded slopes in a finite-dimensional target subspace and strict interior range, so its linearization is compact by the cited criterion. More directly, its normalized evaluation slopes are integrals of Dδ on the compact closed radius-r finite-dimensional range ball, applied to bounded vectors of the same subspace. They lie in the closed absolutely convex hull of a norm-compact set; the normalized slopes generate the free-space unit ball by polarity. A uniform Cauchy bound for D²δ on the radius-r ball, using the positive distance 1−r to the boundary, and the chain rule give the upper bound C_N+K_r Cη_N on the truncation error, with η_N→0. For the matching lower bound, the unit evaluation derivatives at the near-norming ze_j map under βT to φ'_j(z)e_j. After passing to a subsequence any compact perturbation has norm-convergent barycenters, whose escaping coordinates vanish. This proves the lower bound even against compact operators that are not linearizations. The weak-compactness inputs apply to the stated spaces and geometry; for p=1 the lower-bound vectors also disprove weak compactness if the limsup is positive, by the Schur property after applying β. The j² monomials realize the entire range, including zero, since their norms and tails are bounded by the convergent j^{-2} series. Inspected check_diag.py without executing it; its bounded numerical checks of the examples are not the proof.

value.rationale: The Calkin norm is a natural refinement of the known compactness criterion. This formula quantifies exactly what is lost by compact approximation even when the symbol itself has precompact range, and its continuum of examples distinguishes weakly compact operators with every possible normalized norm defect in the reflexive setting. It applies to arbitrary coordinate maps satisfying the stated bounds, not just an isolated monomial example.
